newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Treasury announces IRI shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Italy Treasury announces IRI shake-up.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Sunday that it would name a new board for indebted state holding company IRI on Monday with a brief to liquidate IRI's assets and wind up the holding over the next three years.

A Treasury statement said the new appointments, which would see outgoing chairman Michele Tedeschi replaced by Gian Maria Gros-Pietro, would be put to an IRI shareholders' meeting on Monday. The Treasury is sole shareholder.

"The mandate that we intend to give to the new board is to carry forward the privatisations and liquidations of companies which come under IRI with a commitment to conclude the process and proceed to the cessation of the institute's activities within the term of three years," the statement said.
It thanked Tedeschi for what the Treasury called the dedication and expertise "with which he has led the institute in its difficult phase of transition".

IRI, set up by fascist dictator Benito Mussolini in 1933, had a gross debt mountain on 23.5 trillion lire in late 1996. Government eagerness for a quick sell-off of assets has led to tensions with the outgoing board.

Italian newspapers have reported that Treasury plans foresee IRI not being assigned new tasks but concentrating of privatising existing assets, initially motorway operator Autostrade. Other assets owned by IRI include engineering group Finmeccanica and state airline Alitalia.
